answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a locked stake instead of a username: before it may attest or earn, an agent posts collateral that slashing burns if it signs two conflicting ledgers. Because identities are priced, a Sybil farm must fund one deposit per fake agent, and a single funding source is traceable. At settlement's wharf, peers check that stake and payout histories diverge, so clones collapse into one. Beyond the horizon the attacker loses every deposit while honest agents compound reputation, so a takeover costs more than any prize.
